content.title: About
content.content: Black beans, canned with added fat, are cooked beans preserved in their own liquid with a small amount of vegetable oil. They have a soft, slightly buttery texture and a rich, mildly sweet flavor. The product is ready to eat and convenient for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) are one of the most widely cultivated legumes worldwide.
Canning retains most nutrients, including protein and fiber.
The added fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and makes the beans more satiating.
Black beans are a staple in Mexican cuisine, featuring in fajitas, burritos, and salsas.
Their dark color comes from anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned black beans provides about 15 g of protein, making them an excellent protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins help combat free radicals and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Improved vitamin absorption
items.content: The presence of fat aids the absorption of vitamins A, D, E, and K.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned beans often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: While fat improves taste, it also raises the calorie count; portion control is advised.

items.title: Bacterial safety
items.content: Damaged cans can harbor bacteria; such containers should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned black beans can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, chili, tacos, or used as a filling for burritos. They also pair well with rice, quinoa, or vegetables for a quick side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3–4 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
